noPlan.resolution: Run a $0 presale with orders closing on day 7, inside 9 owner hours. Day 1: the owner gets a writer's written terms (0.5 h): $40/post or less, 4 posts within 5 days of an order, paid within 2 days after the owner's Stripe payout, so nothing is advanced against the $0 cap. With no such writer, stop. Day 2: the owner sends 100 Brain-drafted emails in one batch (2.5 h), offering 4 posts for $300 by Stripe link. Proof: at least 5 paid orders by day 7 (5%). That establishes price, demand and conversion, and carries $1,500 gross (5 x $300). The first Stripe payout comes 7-14 days after the first payment, so by day 21 at worst. Each order then takes about 1 h of owner handling (5 h), for 8 h in total. There is no continue-outreach branch, because orders after day 7 may not settle by day 21. Stop: fewer than 5 paid orders by day 7. Then report that $1,500 in 21 days is not reachable with $0 and 9 hours, deliver the orders already taken, and propose a longer window. If 'in my account' means net of the writer's $160 a pack, 11 orders would be needed, which no 9-hour test reaches; that also calls for a longer window

reviews.reasons: The no-plan finding is right on the evidence: none of the four openings has a price buyers are shown to pay (the only blog figure is the eesel rate-guide estimate, which I verified fails scope), no buying signal and no close rate; the marketplace clearance holds (Fiverr 14 days, Upwork 5 days, Stripe first payout 7-14 days) are sourced; DataAnnotation cannot reach $1,500 in 9 owner hours ($20-$50/h x 9 h = $180-$450). Nothing is misstated as a constraint. But the presale it recommends does not carry the target when it passes at its threshold, and it breaks two limits. (1) Proof = 2 paid of 40 (5%); 'continue: email 40 more' gives 80 contacts, i.e. ~4 orders x $300 = $1,200 < $1,500. Five orders are needed, so at 5% the plan needs ~100 contacts, or a proof of >= 3 of 40 with 40 more. (2) No money in: the writer is paid on delivery (within 5 days of an order, ~day 7-11) but Stripe's first payout lands 7-14 days after the first payment (day 13-20), so $160 a pack must be advanced before any receipt is in the account - exposure above the $0 cap. The writer's terms must be payment after the Stripe payout, or the fulfilment check must require it. (3) Owner hours: 3 h/week x 3 weeks = 9 h. Outreach 2 h + quotes 0.5 h + a second 40 emails ~2 h + 1.5 h per sale x 5 = 7.5 h comes to ~12 h, over the 9 h allowed; the test plan should fit the hours or say it cannot.
findings: Arithmetic: $1,500 / $300 = 5 orders; 2/40 x 80 contacts = 4 orders = $1,200 - passing the test at its threshold falls short.
Cash/exposure: writer due on delivery (~day 7-11) before the first Stripe payout (day 13-20) means owner capital is advanced, against exposureCap $0.
Owner hours: ~12 h needed against 9 h available; card's 1.5 h per sale for 5 sales alone uses 7.5 h.
Settlement: orders after ~day 12 may not settle by day 21 if paid out on the initial 7-14 day schedule; the continue branch needs a last-order day.
Decisive links named (OFFER_AND_PRICE, CONVERSION, CURRENT_DEMAND) are right; FULFILMENT (writer quote) is also resolved by the test and should stay in the proof.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN remains right and its recommended test now works inside every limit. Recomputed: proof 5 paid of 100 by day 7 = 5 x $300 = $1,500 settled (metric SETTLED_CASH), so passing at threshold carries the target. Settlement: first Stripe payout 7-14 days after the first payment (~day 2-7) lands by day 21 at worst; no orders are taken after day 7, so nothing is counted that could settle late. noPlan.resolution: Run a $0 presale with orders closing on day 7, inside 9 owner hours. Each order then takes about 1 h of owner handling (5 h), for 8 h in total. There is no continue-outreach branch, because orders after day 7 may not settle by day 21. Stop: fewer than 5 paid orders by day 7. Then report that $1,500 in 21 days is not reachable with $0 and 9 hours, deliver the orders already taken, and propose a longer window. If 'in my account' means net of the writer's $160 a pack, 11 orders would be needed, which no 9-hour test reaches; that also calls for a longer window
